purpose: An analog clock bent from cyan glass tube, as if a sign maker built it: twelve tube marks, two tube hands on a hub ring, and one magenta spark running the rim for the seconds. It refuses numerals and a second hand tube.

accent.where: the seconds spark on the rim; the hands and marks are cyan tube

night.recipe: The lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes (the Vinyl precedent); the mat around it, visible on the square device, flips with --face-bg, and night dimming comes from the kiosk brightness. For a dark room the glow option pulls the halo in.

options.intent: full is the neon as designed; soft keeps the tubes and their white cores but pulls the halo in, the setting for a clock by the bed.

antiPatterns.rule: Never paint the neon or the stage with --face-ink or --face-bg
antiPatterns.why: the lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes, like the Vinyl record; the day ink is black and would vanish on it, so only the mat outside the disc reads --face-bg

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the still parts live every frame
antiPatterns.why: nine glow passes per stroke made the drafts cost 17 to 20 ms a frame at 1080; anything that changes at most once a minute goes through N.layer in src/apps/clock/neon/faces/tube.ts or the Pi drops frames

antiPatterns.rule: Do not add a second hand tube
antiPatterns.why: the magenta spark is the seconds; a third tube would compete with the hands and give the dial a second saturated quantity

specless: Drawn on a canvas by src/apps/clock/neon/faces/tube.ts in the shared 1000-unit space. Glowing tube hands, twelve marks of two lengths and a seconds spark have no place in the spec vocabulary of solid hands and two tick rings, so the numbers live in the draw module.
